Subject: OrionBank inference throughput degradation — immediate mitigation plan

Lisa —

Thanks for flagging this. We’re seeing the same signal from our side: dedicated GPU pool for your reservation is saturated and requests are queueing, which is spiking tail latency and producing intermittent 5xx errors. I pulled the initial logs and attached the first snapshot (orion_error_snapshot_20280315.log).

Immediate proposed actions (we can implement within the hour if you authorize):
- Temporary burst authorization: enable +30% headroom on the OrionBank dedicated pool for the next 6 hours to drain queues.
- Fallback routing: shift a controlled percentage (~10–15%) of low-priority traffic to the compatible quantized model (q7b) to reduce token wall-time.
- KV cache priming: preload common prefixes we’ve observed in the last 48h to reduce repeated decoder work.

We need confirmation on burst authorization and an ops contact for any change windows. If we don’t get approval in 30 minutes we’ll start the fallback routing as a conservative measure (will notify before changing model variant).

I’ll loop in Marissa and Priyom for mechanics.

—David

Adding technical notes and a recommended play:

What we observe (ops summary):
- Dedicated pool utilization has sustained >98% GPU duty for the last 18 minutes.
- Backpressure is causing KV cache invalidation spikes and longer model kernel launches on some older nodes (kernel skew).
- Error pattern: transient OOM-style retries on two hosts followed by rate-limit cascades (explains 5xx waveform).

Recommended immediate steps (we can implement now):
1) Fallback routing for screening/aux traffic -> route 12% to q7b model variant (config change only, no model upload).
2) Cold-node isolation: temporarily mark two kernel-skewed nodes out-of-rotation and migrate their active segments (should reduce tail latency).
3) Enable prefix caching for the affected prompt families (we have a quick prime script ready).

Expected outcome: we estimate tail P99 latency drop ~40–55% within 15–25 minutes of implementing steps 1+2. Errors should fall to <0.5% once the queue drains.

I’ll prepare the runbook changes and the rollback steps. If OrionBank confirms they cannot authorize burst, these steps will be sufficient to get them under SLA for the next 24–48 hours while we provision additional reserved headroom.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Exec authorization needed: OrionBank dedicated burst or alternative credit path

Vivek / Jonas —

OrionBank (large payments customer) has a reserved-capacity shortfall right now due to an unexpected surge in inference QPS. We have internal mitigations (fallback routing + node isolation + prefix priming) that will likely restore SLA compliance short-term. However, customer is insisting on burst authorization as they can’t approve overage without procurement sign-off. They’ve asked for an ETA to full recovery if we only apply conservative mitigations.

Ask: authorize a one-time emergency burst (+30% headroom for 6 hours) for OrionBank under emergency billing terms OR authorize offering a temporary credit to cover burst charges while they secure internal approval. If neither is approved they will accept the fallback route but will escalate to their CTO if we don’t provide a credit option.

Risk/Impact:
- Approving burst: increases unit spend on our side this billing period but prevents customer business disruption and escalation.
- Offering credit: reduces near-term revenue and sets a precedent but avoids immediate exec escalation.

I recommend approving the emergency burst for 6 hours; we will revert automatically and bill per the emergency policy. If you prefer credit, I can draft a short credit note.

Time-sensitive: customer is in peak traffic; please advise within 45 minutes.

—David

Update —

We implemented fallback routing (12% to q7b) and isolated two nodes at 10:05 PT; prefix priming completed at 10:22 PT. Observed results:
- Queue depth reduced from 18k -> 2.1k within 20 minutes.
- P99 latency for auth flow down ~48% from peak.
- 5xx error rate reduced to 0.4% over the last 15 minutes.

OrionBank procurement confirmed they cannot sign burst this morning; they asked for a temporary credit if we enabled burst. Given the rapid improvement with conservative mitigations, recommending we hold off on burst authorization for now and continue monitoring for the next 6 hours. If metrics regress, we trigger the burst and mark for credit discussion after the incident.

I’ll keep the runbook and telemetry snapshots attached to the ticket (INF-7219).

—Priyom
